title: The Gravity of New Lagos Anew
premise: Noor Yarrow smuggles memories through orbital customs above New Lagos Anew, a city-state that sells its past to fund the generation ships waiting in high orbit. When a ship that never flew appears on his beacon logs carrying the name of a man who died twenty years ago, Noor is pulled into a conspiracy among the Cryos Trust, the oligarchs deciding which half of humanity sleeps through the jump and which half is left behind. Hunted by customs enforcer Adaeze Okonkwo and blackmailed by Trust fixer Silas Vane, Noor discovers the beacon he maintains is actually a ballot box—recording every hidden memory of everyone the Trust erased from the manifest. In the end, Noor broadcasts the erased names to both worlds, forcing an open lottery as the window closes, and chooses to stay awake with the left-behind rather than sleep among the saved.
about_author: Yara Eastwick is the pen name of a former port archivist who spent a decade cataloguing seized data drives in West African free-trade zones before turning to fiction. She writes near-future stories about people who keep other people's secrets for a living.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: POV Noor. On the night shift aboard relay station Kestrel-9, Noor runs contraband memories inside legitimate cargo and tends a beacon whose commissioning records are mysteriously blank. Beat: quiet competence masking loneliness; he knows every customer's secrets and has none of his own.

chapters.title: Manifest of a Ghost
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Customs audit flags the Meridian Dawn—a ship decommissioned before launch—with Noor's beacon listed as its navigation source and a dead man, Tomas Adeyemi, on the crew roster. Beat: unease curdling into fear as he realizes someone is using his invisible life as cover.

chapters.title: Adaeze
chapters.summary: POV Adaeze Okonkwo, customs enforcer, arrives at Kestrel-9 to trace the ghost manifest. She interviews Noor, who lies smoothly but notices she carries a memory-chip sealed with Trust wax. Beat: cat-and-mouse tension; two professionals each pretending to be routine.

chapters.title: What the Dead Man Paid For
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Following the manifest thread, Noor finds Adeyemi's final purchase: a memory of the Trust's original selection criteria, bought the week he died. Beat: dread deepening into resolve; the ghost ship was fleeing with evidence.

chapters.title: Silas Vane Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Trust fixer Silas Vane boards under diplomatic seal, offering Noor wealth and amnesty if he surrenders the beacon's raw logs. Beat: seduction and menace intertwined; Vane knows Noor's real name, which Noor himself barely remembers.

chapters.title: The City That Sold Its Yesterday
chapters.summary: POV Adaeze. Descending to New Lagos Anew, Adaeze walks the Memory Bazaars where citizens sell childhoods to fund the ships. Beat: melancholy wonder; she begins doubting whether the law she serves protects anyone at all.

chapters.title: Half a Manifest
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Decrypting Adeyemi's purchased memory, Noor sees the first draft of the passenger list: entire districts struck out by hand. Beat: moral vertigo; the corruption isn't theft, it's arithmetic.

chapters.title: Kestrel-9 Burns
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Saboteurs hit the station; Noor escapes with the beacon core while his home and stock burn behind him. Beat: loss and adrenaline; invisibility is over—he's now a man with nothing left to hide behind.

chapters.title: Refuge Among Smugglers
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Hiding in the Undertow, the station's unregistered decks, Noor bargains with fence-matriarch Iya Risi for shelter. Beat: wary community; belonging offered at a price he can't yet name.

chapters.title: Adaeze Closes the Net
chapters.summary: POV Adaeze. Ordered to arrest Noor as a saboteur, Adaeze instead finds forensic proof the fire was Trust work. Beat: crisis of loyalty; she files a false report, her first crime.

chapters.title: The Ballot Box in Orbit
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Iya Risi's techs crack the beacon core: it has been recording every suppressed memory sold in the city for thirty years—an archive of everyone the Trust erased. Beat: revelation; the beacon was never navigation, it was testimony.

chapters.title: Vane's Second Offer
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Vane returns, no longer polite: surrender the core or Adaeze takes the fall for his crimes. Beat: coercion tightening; Noor realizes the Trust will burn anyone to bury the list.

chapters.title: Two Thieves, One Truth
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Adaeze tracks Noor down—but comes to trade information, not cuffs. They compare notes over bad coffee in the Undertow. Beat: reluctant alliance; trust built between natural enemies.

chapters.title: Adeyemi's Daughter
chapters.summary: POV Noor. They locate Amara Adeyemi, living quietly under a bought identity her father purchased with his life. She holds the second half of his evidence. Beat: grief and inheritance; the dead man planned further than anyone guessed.

chapters.title: The Selection Criteria
chapters.summary: POV Adaeze. The combined files reveal the algorithm: the Trust weighted wealth, genetics, and obedience—and quietly reclassified dissidents as 'cargo ballast.' Beat: cold fury; justice outside the law becomes the only option.

chapters.title: Leak Attempt One
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Broadcasting through official channels fails; Vane intercepts and kills their courier, Olu. Beat: first blood; the cost of resistance becomes personal and irreversible.

chapters.title: Iya Risi's Price
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Iya Risi agrees to move the archive through smuggler channels—for ownership of the beacon itself. Beat: hard bargain; Noor must decide what the truth is worth in other people's hands.

chapters.title: Adaeze Is Burned
chapters.summary: POV Adaeze. Her false report unravels; she's suspended and marked. Vane offers her redemption for betraying Noor. Beat: isolation; she chooses exile over betrayal and goes dark.

chapters.title: The Window
chapters.summary: POV Noor. The jump window opens in nineteen days; after that, the ships leave and the archive becomes meaningless history. Beat: ticking clock established; every plan now bends around the countdown.

chapters.title: Ghost Ship Rising
chapters.summary: POV Noor. They find the Meridian Dawn mothballed in a graveyard dock—flight-capable, unregistered, and keyed to Adeyemi's biometrics, which Amara inherited. Beat: hope with teeth; the dead man left them a vehicle for the truth.

chapters.title: Amara's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Amara. Offered a legitimate berth on the flagship if she surrenders her father's files, Amara refuses, joining the conspiracy. Beat: courage across generations; the erased choose to speak.

chapters.title: Vane Tightens
chapters.summary: POV Vane. His POV reveals the Trust's panic: half the board wants to scrub the archive, half wants to steal it. He plays both sides. Beat: villain depth; corruption shown as cowardice dressed as stewardship.

chapters.title: Undertow Uprising
chapters.summary: POV Noor. News of the rigged list leaks in fragments; the unregistered decks riot against Trust security. Beat: chaos and solidarity; the left-behind discover they outnumber the saved.

chapters.title: The Trap at Dock Seven
chapters.summary: POV Adaeze. Retrieving the core from Iya Risi, they walk into a Trust ambush. Iya Risi dies covering their escape. Beat: sacrifice; the price of the alliance comes due.

chapters.title: What Noor Forgot
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Inside the core, Noor finds his own suppressed memory: he was a Trust-selected child whose parents paid to erase him from the list—and from his own mind. Beat: devastating self-revelation; he was always one of the saved who chose not to be.

chapters.title: Midpoint Reckoning
chapters.summary: POV Noor and Adaeze. Grieving and galvanized, they commit to broadcasting the full archive plus the live lottery override from the Meridian Dawn during the departure broadcast. Beat: resolve forged in grief; the plan crystallizes.

chapters.title: Buying Ninety Minutes
chapters.summary: POV Adaeze. Adaeze turns herself in to feed Vane false coordinates, buying time for the ship's refit. Beat: sacrifice and cunning; she weaponizes her own disgrace.

chapters.title: The Core Splits
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Under attack, they split the archive: Amara takes half toward the city's public grid, Noor keeps half aboard the ghost ship. Beat: tension via redundancy; either half alone damns them.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Undertow
chapters.summary: POV Noor. A smuggler ally sells Amara's route to Vane. Her convoy is hit; she goes missing. Beat: despair; the network of belonging bleeds.

chapters.title: Interrogation
chapters.summary: POV Amara. Captured, Amara stalls Vane with a poisoned memory-chip planted in her own cache. Beat: defiance under pressure; the erased fight with what they were forced to forget.

chapters.title: Adaeze Breaks Out
chapters.summary: POV Adaeze. Escaping custody during the riots, Adaeze frees Amara and seizes the Trust's uplink tower. Beat: momentum swinging; the lawless now hold the lawful infrastructure.

chapters.title: Countdown: Three Days
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Final preparations; the ghost ship's systems respond to Noor's beacon codes—the beacon was always meant to fly. Beat: convergence; every thread pulls taut.

chapters.title: Vane's Last Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Vane offers Noor his original berth back—his name restored to the list—if he stands down. Beat: temptation at maximum; everything Noor lost, offered back at the cost of everyone else.

chapters.title: The Broadcast Begins
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Departure day: the Meridian Dawn rises on schedule, hijacking the global feed. Names scroll—every erased citizen, every stricken district. Beat: catharsis igniting; the city stops to watch.

chapters.title: Boarding Action
chapters.summary: POV Adaeze. Trust marines storm the uplink tower; Adaeze holds the transmitter long enough for the full archive to land, taking a mortal wound. Beat: heroic climax; she dies a criminal and lives as a conscience.

chapters.title: The Lottery Override
chapters.summary: POV Noor. From orbit, Noor triggers the open lottery: berths redrawn publicly, the algorithm exposed. The Trust board scatters; crowds storm the docks not in rage but in claim. Beat: triumph with tremors; justice delivered outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: Window Closing
chapters.summary: POV Noor. With minutes left, Noor must board or stay. He sends the beacon core down to the city and gives his seat's override to the crowd below. Beat: the central choice made; he refuses the saved half.

chapters.title: What Stays Behind
chapters.summary: POV Noor and Amara. The ships jump. New Lagos Anew stands battered but awake, holding the full archive of its own memory. Beat: bittersweet dawn; the left-behind inherit themselves.

chapters.title: The Beacon, Recommissioned
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Months later, Noor rebuilds Kestrel-9 as a public archive station; the beacon's commissioning record finally bears a name—his, freely given. Beat: healing; invisibility traded for chosen visibility.

chapters.title: Gravity of New Lagos Anew
chapters.summary: POV Noor. Watching the empty jump point, Noor reflects that gravity is just the pull of what you refuse to abandon. Adaeze's badge hangs by the console; Amara transmits the first honest census. Beat: quiet resolution; belonging, finally, on his own terms.
